blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An LP has the rows x + y <= 10, x >= 7 and y >= 6, with x, y >= 0. What is the least total stretch its phase-1 LP finds?

options.text: 0, since each row on its own is met by some plan
options.says: Phase 1 asks for one plan that meets every row at once; here none does.

options.text: 3, since the floors need x + y >= 13 and the cap allows 10
options.says: Right: whatever x + y is, the cap and the two floors are apart by at least 13 - 10 = 3.

options.text: 13, since the two floor rows add up to 13 in all
options.says: The stretch measures how far the rows disagree, not the size of the floors.

options.text: -3, since the cap is 3 below what the floors need
options.says: Each elastic variable is at least 0, so the total stretch can never be negative.

origin.section: Phase 1 Measures How Far the Rows Are From Agreeing, and Finds a First Vertex When They Do

questions.stem: GLOP returns INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUNDED for a maximization model. You solve the same rows with a zero objective, and GLOP returns OPTIMAL. What is the original model?

options.text: Infeasible, since the first solve found no plan to return
options.says: The zero-objective solve found a plan, so the rows can all be met.

options.text: Optimal, since the second solve proved it has a best plan
options.says: The second solve has a different objective; its optimum says only that a plan exists.

options.text: Unbounded, since a plan exists and one of the two must hold
options.says: Right: the status said infeasible or unbounded, and a feasible plan rules out infeasible.

options.text: Degenerate, since two solves of one model disagree
options.says: Degeneracy is about tight rows at a vertex; it does not explain this status.

origin.section: An Unbounded LP Has a Direction Along Which the Objective Improves Forever

questions.stem: In a tableau, basic variable s3 equals 0 and has entry 2 in the entering column. The other rows with positive entries give ratios 4 and 7. What does this pivot do?

options.text: s3 leaves with ratio 0; the basis changes but the plan does not
options.says: Right: 0 / 2 = 0 is the smallest ratio, so the step has length 0, a degenerate pivot.

options.text: s3 is skipped, since ratio 0 moves nothing; the row with ratio 4 leaves
options.says: Skipping it would step 4 units and drive s3 below zero, out of the region.

options.text: The run stops as unbounded, since a basic variable is already zero
options.says: Unbounded means no row has a positive entry; here three rows do.

options.text: The run stops as optimal, since the value can no longer change
options.says: The value stays put for this pivot only; later pivots can still improve it, as in the lesson.

origin.section: A Degenerate Vertex Has More Tight Rows Than It Needs, and Simplex Can Pivot Without Moving

concepts: reading a status that names two outcomes
the phase-1 value of a small set of rows
a ratio test where one ratio is zero
